movement_source: row 'CET1 capital ratio (Level 2)', column As at 30 Sept 2024 -> column As at 30 Sept 2025
headline: Westpac's APRA Level 2 CET1 ratio was 12.53% at 30 Sep 2025 against 12.49% at 30 Sep 2024 — up just 4 bps (ev-1, ev-35). The bank's own FY-on-FY explanation: "The increase from net profit less the payment of 2024 final ordinary dividend and 2025 interim ordinary dividend, other reserve movements and lower capitalised software balances was offset by higher Total RWA and on market share buybacks" (ev-2, ev-22). CET1 capital rose $1,732m to $56,380m, but RWA rose to $450.0bn from $437.4bn (+3%), driven overwhelmingly by IRRBB RWA up 33% to $37.3bn (ev-4, ev-21, ev-18). Statutory net profit was $6,916m, down 1% (ev-24); ordinary DPS rose to 153c and no special dividend repeated (ev-1 context). Westpac publishes NO full-year CET1 walk — only a Mar-25→Sep-25 walk (+29 bps: net profit 80, 1H25 dividend (58), RWA (12), IRRBB 5, Other 16, capital return (2)) (ev-6), so bar-level FY attribution is not disclosed. Level 1 CET1 12.74% (+5 bps) and internationally comparable 18.28% (+1 bp) are different measures (ev-5).

drivers.narrative: Westpac says the ratio's "increase from net profit" was the principal source of capital (ev-2, ev-22). Statutory net profit attributable to owners was $6,916m in FY25 against $6,990m in FY24, down 1% (ev-24); net profit ex Notable Items was $7.0bn, 2% higher than FY24 (ev-36). The bank publishes no FY-on-FY bpts figure; in the Mar-25→Sep-25 half-walk net profit contributed +80 bps (ev-6).

The bank names "the payment of 2024 final ordinary dividend and 2025 interim ordinary dividend" as the offset to net profit (ev-2), and page 6 says net profit "was largely offset by the payment of dividends" (ev-22). Total FY25 ordinary DPS was 153c (final 77c, interim 76c) versus 151c in FY24, which also carried a 15c special dividend (ev-37). Westpac neutralises the DRP by on-market purchase (ev-38). No FY-on-FY bpts is published; the 1H25 dividend alone cost 58 bps in the half-walk (ev-6).

drivers.columns: As at 30 Sept 2025 minus As at 30 Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Westpac states the capital build "was offset by higher Total RWA", which "increased by $12.6 billion mainly from higher Interest Rate Risk in the banking book (IRRBB) RWA" (ev-2). Total RWA went from $437,430m to $450,048m, +3% (ev-21). Components FY25 vs FY24: IRRBB $27,955m→$37,290m, +33% (ev-18); total credit risk $351,724m→$354,476m, +1% (ev-17); market risk $9,555m→$9,873m (ev-19); operational risk $48,196m→$48,409m, flat (ev-20). Contribution is my arithmetic: FY24 CET1 capital re-based on FY25 RWA.

drivers.bank_label: Interest Rate Risk in the banking book (IRRBB) RWA
drivers.columns: As at 30 Sept 2025 minus As at 30 Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Named by the bank as the main reason total RWA rose: RWA "increased by $12.6 billion mainly from higher Interest Rate Risk in the banking book (IRRBB) RWA" (ev-2). IRRBB RWA rose from $27,955m to $37,290m, +33%, i.e. $9.3bn of the $12.6bn (ev-18). Note this reverses after the window: a $14bn RWA reduction followed the revised APS 117 effective 1 October 2025, of which $7.8bn from the modelled 5-year core deposit duration and $6.2bn from optionality/basis and other methodology changes (ev-39) — worth 39 bps as a post-30-Sep-25 adjustment (ev-11, ev-34). Sub-driver of the total-RWA bar; not additive to it.

drivers.columns: As at 30 Sept 2025 minus As at 30 Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Credit RWA rose only 1%, from $351,724m to $354,476m (ev-17), despite gross loans up 6% to $856.4bn and Business lending up 15% and Institutional up 17% (ev-40, ev-41). Within the second half the bank attributes a $12.6bn increase from higher lending "primarily in Corporate and Large Corporate", offset by $5.9bn from model updates, methodology and policy changes and other data refinements, $3.0bn from residential mortgage delinquency improvements, $1.8bn FX translation and $0.8bn credit valuation adjustments (ev-42) — a half-year, not FY, split. Sub-driver of the total-RWA bar.

drivers.columns: As at 30 Sept 2025 minus As at 30 Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Essentially unchanged over the year: $48,196m at Sep-24 to $48,409m at Sep-25, printed as a flat "-" movement (ev-20). Westpac gives no reason. A 17 bps benefit from removal of the operational risk overlay is flagged as an adjustment post 30 Sep 25, i.e. outside this window (ev-12, ev-34). Sub-driver of the total-RWA bar.

drivers.columns: As at 30 Sept 2025 minus As at 30 Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Traded market risk RWA rose from $9,555m to $9,873m, +3% (ev-19). For the half the bank attributes a $1.4bn increase "mainly from higher market risk exposures" (ev-42); no FY-specific reason is published. Sub-driver of the total-RWA bar.

drivers.bank_label: other reserve movements and lower capitalised software balances
drivers.narrative: The bank lists "other reserve movements and lower capitalised software balances" among the sources of the increase (ev-2). In the half-walk this line — labelled "Capital deductions and other items", including FX translation impacts — was +16 bps, "mainly from other reserve movements and lower capitalised software balances" (ev-6, ev-16, ev-43). No FY-on-FY bpts is published.

drivers.bank_label: on market share buybacks / Capital return
drivers.narrative: Westpac names "on market share buybacks" as an offset to the FY25 increase (ev-2). No FY-on-FY bpts is disclosed. In the Mar-25→Sep-25 half-walk capital return was (2) bps "due to the on market share buyback" (ev-6, ev-43), a $0.1bn buyback in the half (ev-44); the remaining on-market buyback announced in Nov-23, May-24 and Nov-24 is shown as a further (23) bps under "Other considerations", not yet in the reported ratio (ev-14, ev-34).

notable_items: Notable Items reduced FY25 net profit after tax by $56m (FY24: $123m reduction) — hedging items only; immaterial to the CET1 movement.
FY24 included a 15c special dividend per share not repeated in FY25 (ev-37 context).

disagreements.topic: Which CET1 measure supplies the movement
disagreements.explanation: The task's method specifies the APRA Level 2 (Group) CET1 ratio. Level 1 and the internationally comparable ratio are different measures printed on the same KPI and capital tables and are quoted only as context.

disagreements.topic: Period span of the published CET1 walk
values: Results announcement p29 walk: Mar-25 -> Sep-25, +29 bps
Investor pack p77/p31 walk: Mar-25 -> Sep-25, +29 bps
disagreements.explanation: Both documents publish only a half-on-half CET1 walk. Its bars (net profit 80, dividend (58), RWA (12), IRRBB 5, Other 16, capital return (2)) describe Mar-25 to Sep-25 and are reported as context only, never as FY25-vs-FY24 contributions.

disagreements.topic: RWA walk endpoints on investor pack p78
values: Chart prints a Sep-24 reference bar of 437.4 alongside a Mar-25 start of 449.5
Bars sum from Mar-25 449.5 to Sep-25 450.0
disagreements.preferred: Bars sum from Mar-25 449.5 to Sep-25 450.0
disagreements.explanation: Although Sep-24 appears on the chart, the decomposed bars (credit quality (3.0), lending 12.6, counterparty credit and MTM (0.7), data refinement (5.9), FX (1.8), IRRBB (2.0), operational (0.1), market 1.4) sum only across the half, so the FY-on-FY RWA split had to be taken from the p30 table columns instead.

limitations: Westpac publishes NO Sep-24 to Sep-25 CET1 walk in either document. Only the Mar-25 to Sep-25 walk is charted (results announcement p29; investor pack p31 and p77), so no bar-level FY25-vs-FY24 attribution exists in the bank's own disclosure. Earnings, dividend, deductions and buyback drivers are therefore left unquantified.

The (35) bps total-RWA contribution is MY arithmetic: FY24 CET1 capital of $54,648m divided by FY25 RWA of $450,048m against FY24 RWA of $437,430m. Westpac does not print an FY-on-FY bps figure for RWA, so this is capped in confidence and the capital-generation side is left unquantified rather than derived to force a sum.

Residual of roughly +39 bps is the unquantified net of earnings, dividends, other reserve/software deductions and buybacks. It is not a published figure; it is the difference between the +4 bps movement and my computed (35) bps RWA drag.

The FY-on-FY IRRBB RWA increase of $9.3bn largely REVERSES after the balance date: the revised APS 117 effective 1 October 2025 cuts RWA by $14bn, shown as a +39 bps CET1 adjustment 'post 30 Sep 25'. The reported 12.53% therefore understates the run-rate ratio on the new standard.

The remaining on-market buyback previously announced in Nov-23, May-24 and Nov-24 is disclosed as a further (23) bps under 'Other considerations', i.e. NOT yet reflected in the 12.53%. Only $0.1bn of buyback ((2) bps) was executed in the second half.

The FY25 total dollar value of buybacks executed during the year, and the FY-on-FY DRP neutralisation amount, are not disclosed in either document, so the capital-returns driver cannot be sized for the task window.

No divestment, acquisition, capital-floor or model-change bps impact is disclosed inside the FY24-to-FY25 window; the pack notes the standardised floor is 'met' but gives no bps. These taxonomy drivers are therefore absent rather than zero.

Both documents in the corpus are the same FY25 results release, so corroboration is within one reporting event rather than genuinely independent; no FY24 book was available to check restatement of the 12.49% comparative.
Basis normalised from 'cash' to 'ex_notables': no page in evidence prints 'cash' beside the movement, and the registry names ex_notables as the bank's headline basis.
No published walk covers FY25 vs FY24: the bank's walk for this metric describes another comparison, so the driver split is not walk-verified for this comparison. Confidence is capped at 85.
